image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a white ceramic bowl containing fresh figs and flower petals. One whole green fig with brown speckles sits at the top left. A halved fig revealing pink/amber flesh and seeds is at the bottom left. White lily-like petals are scattered on the right side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pear-shaped fruit with soft, thin skin in green, purple, or brownish coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whole fruit exhibits the characteristic green skin with brownish speckling typical of ripe figs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Smooth to slightly wrinkled texture with matte finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin appears smooth with a natural matte sheen, consistent with real fruit photography.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated pear shape with tapered form from broad base to narrow stem end.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whole fig displays the correct globular-to-pear morphology with a visible stem attachment point.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small ostiole (eye) at bottom of fruit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bottom of the whole fig is obscured by the angle and the cut fig; the cut fig's orientation does not clearly show the ostiole.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Narrow stem end contrasting with broad rounded base.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The stem end of the whole fig is visible and correctly proportioned relative to the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thin, easily bruised skin covering soft interior.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The transition from skin to flesh in the cut section looks natural and physically consistent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cut cross-section reveals hollow interior filled with numerous tiny seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The halved fig clearly shows the internal structure with many small seeds embedded in the pulp.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Sweet, pink to amber-colored fleshy pulp surrounding seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The color gradient from the outer white rind to the deep amber/pink center is accurate for a ripe fig.
The visual rendering of the pulp suggests a moist, soft consistency rather than a dry or solid one.

artifact_observations.location: White flower petals on the right
artifact_observations.reasoning: The petals have a slightly waxy, plastic-like sheen that differs subtly from the organic translucency expected in real lily petals, though it could be lighting.
Standard depth-of-field blur, but the transition between the sharp foreground fig and the background is very abrupt, typical of AI generation.

selected_experts.reason: Verify species-level classification of the fruit to ensure it is a true fig and not a look-alike.
Confirm the internal seed pattern and pulp color match the biological reality of a fig cross-section.
Check for edge bleeding between the moist fig surface and the dry petals/bowl, a common AI artifact.
Assess overall lighting consistency and detect subtle texture smearing in the high-gloss areas.

focus_areas: Internal seed distribution realism in the cut fig
Boundary sharpness between the wet fig flesh and dry petals
Skin texture micro-details on the whole fig
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'plastic' look of the white petals. While the fig itself looks strong, AI often struggles with the specific translucency of flower petals next to opaque fruit. Verify if the seed pattern in the cut fig is randomly distributed (natural) or repetitive/grid-like (AI artifact).
